new_task_1.title: Warn when version ranges are used in package-scoped profile and CLI patterns that ignore them
new_task_1.description: Conan 2.25.0 adds explicit risk warnings when users place version ranges inside package-scoped pattern positions for profile settings, options, tool requirements, and command-line profile arguments. Those ranges still have no effect in these contexts, but the warning now makes the ineffective input visible instead of silently accepting it.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan warns users when they write package-scoped profile or command-line patterns with version ranges in contexts where those ranges are ignored, so ineffective selectors are no longer silently accepted.

expectation.grounded: When parsing profile `[tool_requires]` entries, profile `[settings]` entries, package-scoped options declarations, or package-scoped `-s`/`-o`/`-c` style profile arguments, Conan should detect a left-hand package pattern containing `[` and emit a risk warning that version ranges have no effect in that context and that only `&` for the consumer and `*` as a wildcard are supported. The underlying setting, option, tool-require, or command-line item should still be parsed and applied with the existing semantics rather than failing.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be told when they are trying to target settings, options, tool requirements, or package-scoped profile arguments with a version range selector that Conan does not actually honor there. The command should keep working, but the warning should make it clear that the range portion is ineffective.

constraints.grounded: Do not turn these inputs into hard errors. Existing package-scoped profile and command-line declarations must continue to parse, and valid special patterns such as `&` for the consumer and `*` as a wildcard must remain supported. The warning should be scoped to the contexts where version ranges are ineffective instead of being emitted generically for all reference matching.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve feedback without changing how these settings are ultimately interpreted. Existing workflows should remain compatible, but misleading selectors should no longer pass without a visible warning.

behavior: A profile `[tool_requires]` pattern that includes a version range now emits a risk warning explaining that the range has no effect in that context.
A profile `[settings]` package pattern that includes a version range now emits a risk warning explaining that the range has no effect in that context.
A package-scoped option pattern that includes a version range now emits a risk warning explaining that the range has no effect in that context.
Package-scoped command-line profile arguments such as `-s`, `-o`, or `-c` now emit the same style of warning when their package pattern includes a version range.
After warning, Conan still accepts and applies the declaration using the existing non-version-range matching semantics for these contexts.
acceptance_criteria: When a user loads a profile containing `[settings]` entries like `pkg/[*]:compiler.cppstd=17`, Conan should emit a warning that the version range in the pattern has no effect and continue processing the profile.

When a user loads a profile containing `[options]` entries like `pkg/[*]:shared=True`, Conan should emit a warning that the version range in the pattern has no effect and continue processing the profile.

When a user loads a profile containing `[tool_requires]` entries like `pkg/[*]:tool/1.0`, Conan should emit a warning that the version range in the pattern has no effect and continue processing the profile.
When a user passes package-scoped `-s`, `-o`, or `-c` arguments whose left-hand pattern contains a version range, Conan should emit a warning instead of silently accepting the ineffective range.
When these warnings are emitted, the command should not fail solely because of the ineffective version range, and matching should still behave according to the supported `&` and `*`-based semantics.
